name: SORT
description: SORT returns a dynamic array of a range or array sorted by one of its columns or rows, in ascending or descending order.
tldr: Sorts a range or array (spills the result).

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array to sort.

parameters.name: sort_index
parameters.description: The column (or row, when by_col is TRUE) number to sort by. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: by_col
parameters.description: FALSE to sort down rows (default) or TRUE to sort across columns.

basicExample.description: Sort a list of numbers ascending
basicExample.result: Sorted list of the values in A2:A10, smallest to largest
basicExample.explanation: With no extra arguments, SORT orders the first column ascending and spills the result.

advancedExamples.title: Sort a table by a specific column
advancedExamples.scenario: Sort a table by the Score column (column 3) from highest to lowest.
advancedExamples.result: The rows of A2:C20 reordered by Score, highest first
advancedExamples.explanation: sort_index 3 picks the third column and -1 sorts it descending.

advancedExamples.title: Sort horizontally
advancedExamples.scenario: Sort values across a single row left to right.
advancedExamples.result: The cells A2:F2 reordered into ascending order
advancedExamples.explanation: by_col TRUE makes SORT sort across columns instead of down rows.

howItWorks: SORT produces a dynamic array containing the sorted values of the input. By default it sorts the first column (or row) ascending. sort_index selects which column/row to sort by, sort_order is 1 (ascending) or -1 (descending), and by_col switches between sorting down rows and across columns. The result spills into neighboring empty cells.

howToSteps.name: Select the source
howToSteps.text: Pick the range or array to sort.

howToSteps.name: Ensure spill space
howToSteps.text: Leave empty cells below/right for the results.

limitations: Available only in Microsoft 365 (and Excel 2021+); not in Excel 2019 and earlier.
Requires empty spill space below/right or it returns #SPILL!.
Sorts by a single key column at a time; use SORTBY for multiple sort keys.

commonErrors.cause: There is no room for the spilled results.
commonErrors.fix: Clear the cells in the spill range.

commonErrors.cause: sort_index points beyond the number of columns/rows.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure sort_index is within the array dimensions.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SORT is available natively in Google Sheets with a similar signature: SORT(range, sort_column, is_ascending, ...).
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Sheets uses separate sort_column and is_ascending pairs and supports multiple keys directly in SORT; by_col is not a parameter.

faq.question: Is SORT available in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, SORT is a native function in Google Sheets.

faq.question: How do I sort descending?
faq.answer: Add -1 as the sort_order argument, e.g. =SORT(A2:A10, 1, -1).

faq.question: Can I sort by multiple columns?
faq.answer: Use SORTBY for multi-key sorting, or supply multiple columns in Sheets' SORT.
